title: Ramayana Becomes Biggest Hindi Film Ever in Kerala With Rs 21 Crore in Six Days
excerpt: Trade trackers say the Nitesh Tiwari epic has passed Dhurandhar: The Revenge's Rs 19.5 crore in Kerala, becoming the first Hindi film to cross Rs 20 crore in the state.
body:
• Ramayana: Part 1 has collected about Rs 21 crore gross in Kerala in six days, passing Dhurandhar: The Revenge's Rs 19.5 crore to become the biggest-grossing Hindi film ever in the state, according to trade trackers.
  • It is the first Hindi film to cross Rs 20 crore in Kerala; the figures are tracker estimates, not certified collections, and reports put the six-day total between Rs 20 crore and Rs 21.05 crore.
  • Pinkvilla reports the film's South dubbed versions together grossed Rs 125 crore in six days, the highest ever for an original Hindi film.
  • The Hindi-language epic, directed by Nitesh Tiwari and starring Ranbir Kapoor, Yash and Sai Pallavi, released worldwide on November 5 and is in theatres now.

Ramayana: Part 1 has become the highest-grossing Bollywood film in Kerala in just six days, a market where Hindi films have historically struggled. According to figures shared by industry tracker AB George and reported by Filmibeat, the film collected approximately Rs 3.80 crore in Kerala on Tuesday, taking its six-day total to Rs 21.05 crore gross and past the Rs 19.50 crore reported lifetime collection of Dhurandhar 2 in the state.

The numbers, and how they compare

The day-wise Kerala figures reported from AB George's tracking are Rs 3 crore on opening day, Thursday, November 5, then Rs 2.15 crore, Rs 3.60 crore, a high of Rs 4.60 crore on Sunday, Rs 3.90 crore on Monday and Rs 3.80 crore on Tuesday. 123Telugu put the six-day Kerala total at Rs 21 crore against the same Rs 19.5 crore previous record, while Pinkvilla reported Rs 20 crore for Kerala over the same period. The trackers differ slightly, and all of these are trade estimates rather than certified collections, but every report agrees on the outcome: the previous record fell inside a week.

"123Telugu put the six-day Kerala total at Rs 21 crore against the same Rs 19.5 crore previous record, while Pinkvilla reported Rs 20 crore for Kerala over the same period."

For scale, the earlier Hindi benchmarks in Kerala were far lower. Pinkvilla's ranking lists Jawan at Rs 13.40 crore and Pathaan at Rs 13.10 crore in the state, behind Dhurandhar: The Revenge at Rs 19.50 crore. AB George's milestone history traces the climb: PK first crossed Rs 5 crore in Kerala in 2014, Dangal crossed Rs 10 crore in 2016, and Dhurandhar 2 took the mark past Rs 15 crore earlier in 2026 before Ramayana became the first Hindi film past Rs 20 crore.

Why Kerala took to it

123Telugu reported that the film faced capacity constraints in Kerala and Tamil Nadu in its first days, with supply not meeting demand, and that it did so without a local promotional push by the team. The reports credit word of mouth and the presence of Yash and Sai Pallavi, both of whom have large followings in the South, alongside Ranbir Kapoor in the lead.

The Kerala record is part of a wider southern run. Pinkvilla reported that the film's dubbed versions in the South grossed Rs 125 crore (Rs 104.50 crore nett) in six days, the highest ever for an original Hindi film, and that Ramayana has also become the highest-grossing Bollywood film in Karnataka.

About the film

Ramayana: Part 1 is a Hindi-language mythological epic directed by Nitesh Tiwari, who co-wrote the screenplay with Shridhar Raghavan. Ranbir Kapoor plays Rama, Yash appears as Ravana in his Hindi film debut, Sai Pallavi plays Sita, Ravi Dubey plays Lakshman and Sunny Deol features as Hanuman. The film is produced by Namit Malhotra and Yash, presented by Prime Focus Studios with Monster Mind Creations, with music by Hans Zimmer and A. R. Rahman and global distribution by Sony Pictures Entertainment. It released worldwide on November 5 and is playing in theatres, including in the United States. The first instalment covers the early chapters of the epic, from Rama's childhood to the start of his 14-year exile.
